messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: More circular-related thoughts
parts:
Hi again,

While looking at my previous problem, I came to think about circular
data some more. This raised questions that I mostly just transcribe
here, hoping that the collective brain of the ggplot community will
compensate the shortcomings of mine.

1/ order of data vs. shortest path:

Please consider this plot:

d <- data.frame(angle=c(pi/2, 2*9*pi/10, pi/10), value=1:3)
ggplot(d, aes(x=angle, y=value)) + geom_path() +
geom_text(aes(label=value)) + coord_polar() +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,2*pi))

should the line between 2 and 3 go through 0 or go the long way
around, as it does now? Is there a way to decide?

2/ data of class circular

As far as I can tell, the standard class for circular data in R is
circular(), form the package of the same name. There are still a few
issues with the basic functioning of the class (e.g. definition of
simple arithmetic operations) because the class was mostly developed
for "high level" work, with specialized functions. However, the
developer has been quite reactive with me so far. It would be nice to
have support for circular data in ggplot. How/where would it be
possible to test whether x or y is of class circular and to call
coord_polar() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, 2*pi)) automatically?

3/ pretty.circular() ?

On the plot above, you can remark that the x axis breaks are not
adapted to the fact that x is an angle. One would rather see: 0, pi/2,
pi and 3pi/2 as major grid lines. But of course these would not make
sense when the variable mapped to x is not an angle. Yet, maybe some
heuristic function could help to guess that (if the range if the data
is close to 0,2pi or 0,360, then chances are that x is an angle). Or
an option is possible, again. Finally, if the circular class is
integrated, there is a direct way of knowing when data is an angle.
In all these cases, having a pretty function adapted to angles would
be nice. I suggest

pretty.circular <- function(x, n=4, unit=c("radians", "degrees"), ...) {
units <- match.arg(units)
if (is.circular(x)) {
units <- circularp(x)$units
}
breaks <- (1:n-1)*pi/n
if (units == "degrees") {
breaks <- round(breaks * 180 / pi)
}
return(breaks)
}

and welcome feedback.

Thanks in advance,

JiHO

That's not currently possible in the ggplot2 framework - the data type
can affect the choice of scale, but not the choice of coordinate
system. (This would also be useful for longitude and latitude if they
had a specific class).

However, it would be possible to create a new circular position scale,
and also provide a circular setting to coord_polar. I think the code
from your previous plot is basically the way I'd go about it.

sure if inspecting circular units will be sufficient in general - what
happens if you have two layers with different units?)
